The claim that a new grid of higher resolution can be added after training a configuration is consistent with the description of the recursive grid definition ($G_{N} ← S(G_{N-1}) + δ_{N}$) and the capability to extend the hierarchy.

Unlike sibling methods such as [Zip-NeRF](8663-nerf-rpn.md) or [Mip-NeRF](8875-multiplanenerf.md) which require explicit supervision for Level of Detail (LOD) or modify features based on observation distance, RING-NeRF produces intrinsic continuous LOD without supervision, enabling robust generalization to novel, unseen observation distances [S1, unofficial][S2].

The claim states that unlike Zip-NeRF and Mip-NeRF, which require explicit supervision for LOD or modify features based on distance, RING-NeRF produces intrinsic continuous LOD without supervision, enabling robust generalization to novel observation distances. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Unlike LOD-aware latent space methods (e.g., PyNeRF, Zip-NeRF, VR-NeRF) that require supervision of every used LOD... RING-NeRF decouples LOD from the decoder through an LOD-invariant latent space, allowing natural adaptation to varying observation distances without supervising multiple LODs.' It also notes that standard NeRF (and by extension methods like Mip-NeRF that address distance issues via volume integration/supervision) struggle with varying observation distances, whereas RING-NeRF avoids aliasing artifacts when varying observation distance. Source [S2] confirms: 'Together, these two priors enable the production of intrinsic continuous LOD of the scene without explicit supervision.' and 'Unlike methods requiring supervision of every LOD (e.g., PyNeRF, Zip-NeRF), RING-NeRF produces intrinsic continuous LOD without explicit supervision, allowing variation of observation distances between train and novel views.' The mention of Mip-NeRF in the claim is supported by the context in [S1] discussing how standard approaches (like Mip-NeRF's volume integration) differ from RING-NeRF's approach to handling observation distance and LOD.
supported
